summary: We are testing whether an adaptive-budget Simulated Annealing + Iterated Local Search approach (capping total SA iterations at 1.5M and scaling restart count by graph size) eliminates the time-limit-exceeded (TLE) failures observed in iteration 2's fixed 12-restart SA+ILS, while maintaining or improving Max-Cut quality (target score ≥ 87.0 out of 100).
key_points: Main arm: Adaptive SA+ILS with 1.5M total iteration budget, fewer restarts for large graphs (5 for n>600), 30 ILS perturbation cycles per restart, greedy/random initialization mix. Prediction: score ≥ 87.0 with no TLE-induced zeros.

Control arm: Iter-2's fixed 12-restart SA+ILS (≈3M total iterations). Prediction: score variance ≥ 3 points due to TLE on large test cases, confirming that the fixed restart count is the root cause of inconsistency.

Confirmation criteria: If the adaptive arm scores ≥ 87.0 and the control arm scores lower or shows variance, the hypothesis that adaptive work scaling fixes TLE is confirmed. Refutation: if adaptive arm scores < 87.0 (budget too tight or fewer restarts hurt diversity) or if the control arm scores comparably well (TLE was not actually the bottleneck).
